# Volume 3 — Chapter V Letters from Home

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

During the subsequent three weeks, Nell and Honora persisted in feeling like strangers in an unfamiliar territory. Subsequently, all at once, every element appeared to align—Wexcombe, professors, classes, students, studies, and social activities. Rather than consisting of isolated pieces, life grew unified once more. The Freshmen, no longer an assemblage of disconnected people, realized they were a class, possessing a class spirit, a class yell, class interests, class antipathies, and class ambitions. Victory belonged to them in the yearly “Arts Rush” against the Sophomores, through which they acquired the esteem of every class, alongside a huge, confidence-instilling self-image. The Sophomores had emerged victorious in the “rush” for three years; the fact that this year's triumph rested on the Freshmen's banner was credited to the tactical leadership of Hugh Carrow, who organized the operation and devised particular novel methods, which disrupted the Sophs and propelled the Freshmen to success. Due to his recognized merit, he was chosen as president of the Freshman Class, a prestigious and responsible office—at minimum, from a Fresh perspective—desired by numerous individuals. Furthermore, he received an invitation to enter the “Lambs”—Redmondese denoting Lamba Theta—an honor seldom offered to a Freshman. Before the initiation, as a trial, he was required to march through the primary commercial thoroughfares of Portmaris throughout an entire day while dressed in a sunbonnet and a large kitchen apron made of brightly patterned calico. He performed this gladly, tipping his sunbonnet with polite elegance whenever he encountered women he knew. Wilfred Mott, who had failed to receive an invitation to join the Lambs, remarked to Nell that he could not understand how Carrow was able to perform such an act, and that he himself could never degrade himself in that manner.
{: #nw-v03-c05-p0000 }

“Envisioning Wilfred Mott adorned in a calico apron together with a sunbonnet makes me giggle,” Honora giggled. “He would bear a total resemblance to his aged Grandmother Mott. Hugh, by contrast, appeared just as manly wearing those items as he did dressed in his own suitable attire.”
{: #nw-v03-c05-p0001 }

Nell and Honora became deeply involved in the social scene of Wexcombe. Cressida Lindsay was largely responsible for this happening so quickly. As the daughter of a wealthy and prominent man, Cressida hailed from an established and elite “Bluenose” lineage. Because of this, as well as her beauty and charm—a charm recognized by everyone who crossed her path—the doors to every clique, club, and class in Wexcombe were instantly thrown open to her; and Nell and Honora accompanied her wherever she went. Cressy “adored” Nell and Honora, particularly Nell. Possessing a loyal nature, she was entirely free from any sort of snobbery. “Love me, love my friends” appeared to be her implicit rule. Effortlessly, she brought them along into her constantly expanding realm of acquaintances, making the social journey at Wexcombe extremely smooth and enjoyable for the two Brierley girls, which sparked the envy and amazement of the other freshettes who, missing Cressida’s backing, were destined to stay mostly on the sidelines during their initial year at college.
{: #nw-v03-c05-p0002 }

For Nell and Honora, who held graver outlooks on existence, Cressy was still the entertaining, endearing infant she appeared to be when they initially met. Nevertheless, as she declared on her own behalf, she possessed “heaps” of intellect. The moment or location in which she discovered opportunity to read was an enigma, because she appeared constantly sought after for a variety of “fun,” and her domestic nights were packed with visitors. She possessed every one of the “beaux” that a soul might wish for, because nine-tenths of the Freshmen alongside a large portion of every other class competed for her favor. She felt innocently thrilled about this state of affairs, and joyfully detailed every additional triumph to Nell and Honora, offering remarks that could have caused the unfortunate suitor’s ears to sting intensely.
{: #nw-v03-c05-p0003 }

“It appears that Hector and Orlando have no major competitor so far,” Nell observed playfully.
{: #nw-v03-c05-p0004 }

“Not a single one,” Cressida concurred. “Every week I send letters to both of them, sharing all the details regarding my local young men. It undoubtedly amuses them, I feel certain. Nevertheless, naturally, the single one I favor most is unattainable for me. Hugh Carrow ignores me completely, save for gazing at me like I am an agreeable little kitten he wants to stroke. I am all too aware of the cause. Queen Nell, I hold a grievance against you. Truthfully, hating you is what I should be doing, yet I adore you passionately instead, and failing to behold you daily leaves me wretched. No other girl I ever met previously compares to you. Whenever your eyes meet mine in a particular manner, I sense just how unimportant, silly, and little a creature I am, inspiring me to become superior, more intelligent, and stouter of heart. Following that, I form firm intentions; however, the very first handsome chap who crosses my path shatters every one of them from my mind. Isn’t the life at college splendid? It is quite comical reflecting on how I loathed it during that initial day. Yet had I not, my friendship with you might never have truly formed. Nell, do repeat once more that I am liked by you even a small amount. Hearing it is my deep longing.”
{: #nw-v03-c05-p0005 }

“I adore you quite a lot—and to me you seem like a precious, gentle, delightful, soft, harmless, tiny—feline,” Nell chuckled, “yet I fail to understand how you ever manage to find the hours for studying your schoolwork.”
{: #nw-v03-c05-p0006 }

Cressy must have discovered the time, because she maintained her standing in all her year's classes. Even the ill-tempered, elderly Mathematics professor, who hated female students and had fiercely fought their entry into Wexcombe, was unable to stump her. She guided the freshettes in all areas, apart from English, in which Nell Harcourt surpassed her by a wide margin. Nell herself discovered that the coursework of her Freshman year was quite simple, largely owing to the consistent labor she and Hugh had performed over those prior two years in Brierley. Consequently, she had additional time for a social life that she immensely appreciated. Yet she never forgot Brierley and her friends there for a single instant. For her, the most joyful times of every week were the ones when mail arrived from home. Only after receiving her initial letters did she start believing she might ever enjoy Portmaris or feel comfortable there. Prior to their arrival, Brierley had appeared thousands of miles distant; those letters brought it close and bound the past life to the present one so intimately that they started to appear as a single continuous existence, rather than two completely isolated lives. That initial group comprised six letters, written by Odette Pullen, Opal Pettigrew, Isolde Pembroke, Thirza, Mrs. Sowerby, and Robin. The letter from Odette was a copperplate piece of penmanship, featuring every “t” carefully crossed and every “i” accurately dotted, yet it lacked a single captivating sentence. She made no reference to the school, about which Nell was desperate to learn; she responded to none of the inquiries Nell had posed in her correspondence. Instead, she informed Nell about the number of yards of lace she had lately crocheted, as well as the local weather in Brierley, her plans for the construction of her new dress, and her sensations whenever her head throbbed. Opal Pettigrew composed an effusive letter grieving over Nell’s departure, promising her that she was terribly missed in all activities, inquiring about the nature of the Wexcombe “fellows,” and occupying the remainder with stories of her own distressing encounters with her many suitors. It was a foolish, innocent letter, and Nell would have found it amusing if not for the postscript. “Hugh seems to be enjoying Wexcombe, judging from his letters,” wrote Opal. “I don’t think Wilfred is so stuck on it.”
{: #nw-v03-c05-p0007 }

Hugh was corresponding with Opal, then! That was fine. Naturally, he possessed every right to do so. Except—!! Nell was unaware that the initial letter had been sent by Opal and that Hugh’s reply was prompted by plain politeness. Disdainfully, she threw Opal’s note to the side. However, erasing the sharpness of Opal’s postscript required the entirety of Isolde’s lively, informative, and charming communication. Although Isolde’s page mentioned Gideon slightly too often, it was otherwise packed and overwritten with engaging news, making Nell feel nearly returned to Brierley as she perused it. Thirza provided a somewhat formal and muted message, strictly devoid of any rumors or sentiment. Nevertheless, it somehow brought to Nell a breath of the pure, unpretentious existence at Grey Shutters, carrying its hint of old-world quiet and the constant, enduring affection waiting for her there. Mrs. Sowerby’s communication proved packed with parish updates. Because she had disbanded her home, Mrs. Sowerby enjoyed extra leisure to give to religious matters, throwing her whole heart and soul into them. Currently, she felt quite agitated regarding the inferior “supplies” filling the empty Brierley pulpit.
{: #nw-v03-c05-p0008 }

“Only blockheads join the clergy these days, in my opinion,” was her resentful inscription. “The applicants provided to us are terrible, and their sermons are total nonsense! A good portion is false, and even more concerning, it strays from orthodox teaching. Our current minister represents the absolute lowest point. His usual habit is selecting a scripture only to speak on an unrelated topic. Furthermore, he claims a disbelief in the everlasting damnation of every pagan. Imagine that! Should they escape perdition, all of our financial contributions toward Foreign Missions are utterly thrown away, mark my words! During the previous Sunday evening service, he made an announcement that his upcoming sermon would focus on the swimming iron axe-head. My view is that he ought to stick strictly to the Scriptures and refrain from choosing theatrical topics. Conditions are truly shameful when a preacher fails to discover sufficient material within Sacred Scripture to discuss, mark my words. Which place of worship do you frequent, Nell? It is my desire that your attendance is consistent. Individuals frequently become indifferent regarding religious services when distant from their households, and my knowledge is that university pupils commit major offenses regarding this matter. Information has reached me that a large number of them truly complete their schoolwork on the Lord's Day. May you never fall to such a disgraceful level, Nell. Keep your upbringing in mind. Additionally, exercise extreme caution regarding the companions you select. One cannot determine what kinds of beasts inhabit those educational institutions. Externally they could resemble whitewashed tombs while internally behaving like predatory wolves, mark my words. It would be wisest for you to completely avoid speaking with any youth who fails to originate from the Island.”
{: #nw-v03-c05-p0009 }

“I neglected to mention to you what occurred on the day the minister paid a visit here. It was the most amusing sight I have ever witnessed. I remarked to Thirza, ‘If Nell had been here wouldn’t she have had a laugh?’ Thirza herself even laughed. You are aware that he is an extremely short, chubby small man with bow legs. Well, that old pig belonging to Mr. Pettifer—the large, tall one—had strayed over here once more that day and forced its way into the yard, and it had entered the back porch, without our knowledge, and it was located there when the minister showed up in the doorway. It executed one frantic charge to escape, but there was no place to charge toward except right between those bow legs. Therefore it went right there, and, since it was so large and the minister so small, it swept him entirely off his feet and bore him off. His hat flew in one direction and his cane in another, right as Thirza and I reached the door. I will never erase the sight of him from my memory. And that unfortunate pig was almost frightened to death. I will never manage to read that narrative in the Bible regarding the swine that charged furiously down the steep slope into the sea without picturing Mr. Pettifer’s pig galloping down the hill bearing that minister. I imagine the pig believed he was carrying the Old Boy on his back rather than within him. I felt grateful the twins were not around. It would not have been proper for them to witness a minister in such an embarrassing plight. Right before they reached the brook the minister leaped off or tumbled off. The pig dashed through the brook like a lunatic and onward through the woods. Thirza and I hurried down and assisted the minister in getting up and dusting his coat. He suffered no injury, but he was furious. He appeared to consider Thirza and me accountable for the entire incident, even though we informed him that the pig was not ours, and had been bothering us the whole summer. Furthermore, why did he approach the back door? You would never have caught Mr. Wace doing such a thing. A considerable amount of time will pass before we find a man like Mr. Wace. Nevertheless, it is an ill wind that blows nobody good. We have not spotted hoof or hair of that pig from that moment on, and I hold the conviction that we never shall.
{: #nw-v03-c05-p0010 }

“Affairs are rather still in Brierley. Grey Shutters does not seem as lonely to me as I anticipated. It is my intention to begin a different cotton warp quilt during this winter. A lovely new apple-leaf design belongs to Mrs. Silas Mott.
{: #nw-v03-c05-p0011 }

“Whenever I need a bit of a thrill, I peruse the murder court cases in the Boston newspaper my niece mails to me. It wasn't my habit past, yet I find them genuinely fascinating. The States has got to be a dreadful region. It is my wish that you won't ever travel there, Nell. However, the manner in which young women wander about the globe these days is truly horrifying. It constantly reminds me of Satan within the Book of Job, traveling back and forth and walking back and forth. I am convinced the Lord never designed it to be so, and that is a fact.”
{: #nw-v03-c05-p0012 }

“Robin has behaved quite well since your departure. He misbehaved one day, so Thirza disciplined him by forcing him to put on Lucy’s apron for the entire day, whereupon he proceeded to chop up every single one of Lucy’s aprons. After I gave him a spanking for doing that, he went off and ran my rooster until it died.
{: #nw-v03-c05-p0013 }

“My residence has become the new home of the MacPhersons. Being a very particular person, she is a wonderful housekeeper. All my June lilies were yanked up by her on the grounds that a garden is made to appear terribly messy by them. At the time of our marriage, Thomas planted those lilies. A pleasant enough fellow describes her husband, yet she is unable to move past having been an old maid, and that is the truth.
{: #nw-v03-c05-p0014 }

“Avoid working too much at your studies, and make certain that you dress in your winter undergarments the moment the temperature drops. Thirza experiences much anxiety regarding you, yet I inform her that you possess considerably more wisdom than I previously anticipated you would acquire, and that you will manage just fine.”
{: #nw-v03-c05-p0015 }

At the very beginning, Robin’s letter descended into a complaint.
{: #nw-v03-c05-p0016 }

“Dearest anne, kindly send a note asking marilla to refrain from fastening me to the bridge rail during my fishing trips since the other boys tease me on those occasions. Living here in your absence feels terribly lonely, though school provides wonderful entertainment. Odette andrews exhibits a nastier disposition than yours. Yesterday evening, I frightened mrs. lynde using a jack-o'-lantern. Her anger was intense, and she became equally enraged because I pursued her elderly rooster throughout the farmyard until he collapsed and perished. Causing his sudden death was not my intention. Nell, what caused his life to end, I am eager to learn. mrs. lynde tossed his body to the pigs when she could have traded him to mr. blair instead. Currently, mr. blair pays 50 cents each for fine deceased roosters. I overheard mrs. lynde requesting the minister's prayers on her behalf. Nell, what dreadful deed did she commit, I am eager to learn. A kite possessing a splendid tail now belongs to me, anne. During class yesterday, Milty bolter shared a marvelous tale with me. The account is accurate. Late one evening last week, old Joe Mosey and Leon engaged in a card game out in the forest. Their playing cards rested upon a tree stump when a colossal dark figure taller than the forest canopy arrived, snatched both cards and stump, and vanished accompanied by a booming sound resembling thunder. They must have been terrified, I am certain. According to Milty, that dark figure was the devil himself. Was it truly him, anne, I am eager to learn. Mr. kimball, who resides in spenservale, suffers from severe illness and must be admitted to the hospitable. Allow me a moment to inquire of marilla whether my spelling is correct. Thirza claims the silem represents his actual destination rather than that first location. He believes a serpent resides within his body. What feeling does housing a serpent in your body produce, anne, I am eager to learn. mrs. lawrence bell has also fallen ill. mrs. lynde asserts that her sole ailment stems from obsessing excessively over her internal organs.”
{: #nw-v03-c05-p0017 }

“What Mrs. Sowerby would make of Cressida,” Nell remarked, putting her letters away, “is something I wonder about.”
{: #nw-v03-c05-p0018 }
